title: Non-blocking follow-up from PR #152 review (frontend-support-resistance-overlay)
description: Tracked non-blocking finding from pr-reviewer's review of PR #152 (frontend-support-resistance-overlay), recorded here per CLAUDE.md's 'every non-blocking finding becomes a tracked task' rule so it isn't lost once that PR merges. Distinct from the PR's own blocking findings (the zone-band price-scale autoscale distortion, and the single-visible-bar setData crash risk), which stay on frontend-support-resistance-overlay itself and must be fixed before that PR can be accepted.

checklist.step:
RESOLVED IN PART by PR #152's retry-round-2 fix (commit 805a3d9, see the parent task's review.comments): supportResistanceZoneHelp/falseBreakoutHelp's interpretValue calls and the legend's visibility gate now consume the same price-relevance-filtered + MAX_DISPLAYED_ZONES=6-capped `displayedZones` (`selectDisplayedZones`) the chart-drawing effect uses, closing the 'nearest zone'/'Showing N of M' mismatch that was blocking on retry rounds 1 and 2 -- independently re-verified live (AAPL/MSFT/AMD/BA/DIS/OKTA, all range/interval combinations, no divergence found; no useMemo anywhere in PriceChart.tsx, so the two computations can't drift by construction). STILL OPEN: falseBreakoutHelp.interpretValue's 'Most recent' reading is filtered by `displayedZones` but is NOT further windowed by the currently-visible date range the way buildFalseBreakoutMarkers' marker and the dashed 'False-breakout stop' price line both are (PriceChart.tsx's `firstDate`/`lastDate` windowing) -- so it can still describe a specific breakout (exact dates + stop price) whose marker/price-line isn't actually rendered in the current range view, even though the zone it belongs to genuinely is. Reproduced live in the retry-round-2 re-review: OKTA at 1M/3M/6M (reentry 2026-01-28, outside those windows) and DIS at 1M/3M (reentry 2026-01-21) show identical false-breakout legend text whether or not the marker/price-line is actually on screen -- confirmed via screenshot that the 1Y/Max views show both while the shorter ranges show neither, with no change in legend text. Judged non-blocking (the retry-round-2 review's own reasoning: the zone itself is genuinely drawn, the fact described is real, and the zone band's own established behavior is likewise range-independent, so there's a legitimate design-tradeoff reading, not a clear-cut bug). Fix direction if picked up: either window falseBreakoutHelp.interpretValue's search to breakouts whose reentry_date falls within the current `firstDate`/`lastDate` (matching the marker/price-line exactly, at the cost of the legend sometimes saying 'no false breakouts in the current view' even though the zone has one outside it), or explicitly caveat the text when the described episode isn't in the current view (e.g. 'not shown at the current range') -- a decision worth recording explicitly given the zone-band precedent argues for leaving it as-is.

RESOLVED (this task): falseBreakoutHelp.interpretValue now takes an `inVisibleRange` parameter (defaulting to `true`), following the exact divergenceHelp/kangarooTailHelp precedent cited above -- it still names the real most-recent episode (among `displayedZones`) in full, and appends an out-of-range caveat clause + a `(not in current range)` legend-label suffix + a dimmed legend swatch when the episode's own `reentry_date` falls outside the current `firstDate`/`lastDate` window. `mostRecentFalseBreakoutZone` was extracted and exported from metricHelpContent.ts so PriceChart.tsx's own `inVisibleRange` computation runs the exact same 'most recent' selection the legend text itself uses (can't drift, same pattern `selectDisplayedZones` already established), and a new shared `isFalseBreakoutInRange` helper (mirroring `isKangarooTailInRange`) replaces the inline windowing checks `buildFalseBreakoutMarkers` and the price-line loop already had. Verified with unit tests (PriceChart.test.tsx, metricHelpContent.test.ts) and a throwaway Playwright screenshot walkthrough (not committed) confirming the legend caveat/dimming and MetricHelp balloon text both appear only when the episode is actually out of the visible range.

The 50%-price-ratio relevance window (isZoneRelevant/ZONE_RELEVANCE_PRICE_RATIO, PriceChart.tsx, added in PR #152 retry-round-1 commit 4f1a1f4) is anchored only to the latest visible close, not to the currently-visible bars' own price span. pr-reviewer's retry-round-1 re-review stress-tested this with a synthetic zone ~40% above the latest close (inside the 50% window, so treated as relevant) against a 1-month preset range: the y-axis stretched to squash the actual candlestick/EMA/channel content into roughly the same fraction of the pane (~11%) as the original reported autoscale-distortion bug -- the same zone against a 1-year view was fine (more natural price spread to absorb it). Real zones are strength-scored independent of price distance, so a strong zone 30-45% from today's price is plausible for some ticker/time even though none of AAPL/NVDA/MSFT/AMD's currently-cached data hit this band during that review. Not blocking (bounded distortion, ~2.25x worst case, and a real tradeoff already reasoned through in that PR's decisions entry) but worth reconsidering: an approach that also accounts for the actually-visible bars' own high/low range (e.g. intersecting the ratio window with a multiple of the visible span), not a fixed ratio off the latest close alone.

RESOLVED (this task): `isZoneRelevant`/`selectDisplayedZones` now take the currently-visible bars' own price span (`visibleBarPriceSpan`: min low/max high across every visible bar, not just first/last) and intersect the existing 50% price-ratio window with a second window built from that span (`ZONE_RELEVANCE_VISIBLE_SPAN_MULTIPLE=2` times the span either side of the visible high/low, floored at `ZONE_RELEVANCE_MIN_VISIBLE_SPAN_RATIO=10%` of the reference price so a near-flat visible range doesn't collapse the window to nothing). Intersecting (never replacing) the ratio window means this can only shrink the eligible window, never widen it, so the worst case is no worse than the already-reasoned-through ratio-only bound. Verified: all pre-existing PriceChart.test.tsx zone-relevance tests pass unchanged (their zones stay within the floored span window), a new unit test confirms a zone ~40% away is now excluded on a narrow 2-bar view that was previously included, and a throwaway Playwright screenshot (not committed) against the running app confirms the axis stays undistorted (212-240 range) with the far zone's band simply absent, rather than the axis stretching to include it.

decisions.decision: falseBreakoutHelp.interpretValue keeps describing the real most-recent false-breakout episode among displayedZones in full, and appends an out-of-range caveat clause (plus a '(not in current range)' legend suffix and a dimmed swatch) when that episode's reentry_date falls outside the currently visible bar range -- it does NOT filter its own search down to only in-range breakouts.
decisions.rationale: Mirrors the exact precedent already established for divergenceHelp/kangarooTailHelp (PR #158/#165, both cited in the checklist item itself): a real, currently-qualifying fact about a zone that IS actually displayed stays worth surfacing even when the current range selection happens to exclude its own historical marker, rather than making the legend claim 'no false breakouts' for a zone that genuinely has one just outside the window. Rejected alternative: windowing the search itself to only reentry_date-in-range breakouts -- this was rejected specifically because it would produce exactly that misleading 'nothing here' reading, and because it would diverge from the app's own established convention for the two structurally identical cases (divergence, Kangaroo Tail) with no principled reason for false breakouts to behave differently. A shared `mostRecentFalseBreakoutZone` helper (exported from metricHelpContent.ts) and `isFalseBreakoutInRange` helper (PriceChart.tsx, mirroring `isKangarooTailInRange`) ensure the legend's caveat decision and the chart's own marker/price-line windowing can never drift apart -- same 'one shared function, not two independently-computed conditions' principle `selectDisplayedZones` already established for the zone list itself.

decisions.decision: The support/resistance zone relevance window (isZoneRelevant) now intersects the existing 50% price-ratio window with a second window derived from the currently-visible bars' own high/low span, expanded by a multiple of 2 either way and floored at 10% of the reference price. Chose to fix this now (not just document it as an accepted limitation) via an intersection (never a replacement) of the two windows, with the floor calibrated so every zone fixture already exercised by PriceChart.test.tsx (all well within the existing 2-bar test fixtures' own narrow span) keeps passing unchanged.
decisions.rationale: An intersection can only ever shrink the eligible window relative to the ratio-only baseline, never widen it, so the worst-case distortion bound already reasoned through in PR #152's own decisions entry can only improve, not regress -- this made the fix low-risk to adopt outright rather than deferring it as 'documented limitation'. The floor (10% of reference price) was chosen, rather than an unfloored raw span multiple, because an unfloored version would have required rewriting most of this file's own zone-relevance test fixtures (which use a synthetic, near-flat 2-bar dataset unrelated to what they're actually testing -- band rendering, the display cap, false-breakout windowing) to give them a more realistic multi-week price span, a much larger and riskier diff for a follow-up task than the concrete distortion bug being fixed warranted. The floor does mean a genuinely flat/quiet real trading window won't get the full tightening benefit this fix otherwise provides, but that's the strictly safer failure mode (falls back toward the pre-existing, already-accepted ratio-only bound) rather than the alternative of an over-tight window hiding zones that are genuinely still relevant. The multiplier (2x the effective span either side) and floor (10%) were picked to keep every pre-existing test passing while still excluding a zone ~40% away from a realistically narrow (non-floor-dominated) visible range, per this task's own throwaway Playwright verification -- not derived from a rigorous distortion-optimality analysis, since no such derivation was available without extensive real-market-data experimentation out of scope for a follow-up task of this size.

review.notes:
Full review per pr-reviewer process, with extra scrutiny given the task's explicit instruction (this touches the exact 'legend/chart data-source mismatch' and 'axis distortion' bug classes that took multiple retry rounds in PR #152).

(1) mostRecentFalseBreakoutZone sharing: read the code directly, not just the claim. metricHelpContent.ts exports mostRecentFalseBreakoutZone; falseBreakoutHelp.interpretValue calls it internally, and PriceChart.tsx's legend render calls the exact same exported function to compute mostRecentBreakoutZone, then checks its reentry_date against isFalseBreakoutInRange -- the same helper buildFalseBreakoutMarkers and the false-breakout price-line loop both use for their own windowing. The legend's `bars` (historyQuery.data.bars.filter(hasFiniteOhlc)) and the chart effect's `finiteBars` (data.bars.filter(hasFiniteOhlc), same historyQuery.data) are computed with the identical filter over the identical source, so firstDate/lastDate match between the two computations by construction, not just by convention. No useMemo/independent recomputation anywhere that could let the two drift. Confirmed live: GOOGL's rank-3 false-breakout zone (reentry 2026-08-17) shows 'False Breakout (not in current range)' + a dimmed dashed swatch + MetricHelp caveat text at the 1M preset, and switches to a plain 'False Breakout' legend with the marker/price-line actually rendered at 3M/6M/1Y/Max -- verified via Playwright screenshots, not just trusting the claim.

(2) Intersection-based relevance window: verified the math -- windowMin = max(ratioMin, spanMin), windowMax = min(ratioMax, spanMax) is a genuine intersection of the pre-existing 50%-ratio window with a new span-based window, so the eligible range can only shrink relative to the ratio-only baseline (never widen it), and since referencePrice is the close of the same bar whose high/low feed visibleBarPriceSpan, referencePrice always lies inside both windows so windowMin<=windowMax never inverts. New unit test (twoBars, a zone ~40% away) confirms exclusion that the old ratio-only window would have let through; all pre-existing zone-relevance fixtures still pass unchanged. Live-verified with TSLA/GOOGL across 1M/3M/1Y/Max: axis stays proportioned to visible content at every preset, no repeat of the ~11%-of-pane squash PR #152's retry-round-1 review reproduced.

(3) Own browser walkthrough: backend started in FINTRADE_DATA_PROVIDER_MODE=fixture (frontend dev server env-cleaned of a stale absolute VITE_API_BASE_URL that was causing CORS failures -- unrelated pre-existing environment artifact, not a PR bug, fixed locally for the walkthrough only, not committed), drove GOOGL and TSLA through every range preset via a throwaway Playwright script (ms-playwright chromium already provisioned). Golden path (false-breakout caveat appears/disappears correctly across ranges, zone bands stay proportioned) and an edge case (a genuinely out-of-range false breakout at the narrowest 1M preset) both confirmed by screenshot; browser console had zero errors throughout.

Static analysis: backend ruff/mypy clean; frontend eslint/tsc -b --noEmit clean. Backend pytest+coverage: 741 passed, 99.92% total (no regression, PR doesn't touch backend). Frontend vitest+coverage: 511 passed, 99.7% statements / 98.89% branches (matches PR's own claims exactly). Persisted e2e suite (`make e2e`): all 16 specs across 4 files passed. code-review skill (medium effort) independently reviewed the same two functional changes and found no correctness bug, removed guard, or CLAUDE.md violation. No new files/components added (no frontend placement question applies). No backend/API changes (OpenAPI snapshot not applicable). Area is frontend/pages/stocks with skill: null, not backend/signals or backend/portfolio, so verify-elder-signal wasn't separately invoked, but the change was checked against docs/Analyse.md's false-breakout section (data/methodology unchanged, this PR only adjusts presentation windowing) and found consistent. No 'decide X' checklist phrasing without a matching decisions entry -- both checklist items have corresponding decisions entries with full rationale. No pre-existing pr_decision on this task to clear. Zero non-blocking findings, so no follow-up task was created.

pr_decision.notes: Independently re-ran `yarn vitest run --coverage --no-file-parallelism`: 511/511 tests passed, 99.7% statements / 98.89% branches -- matches pr-reviewer's numbers exactly (one PortfolioPage.test.tsx timeout in a parallel run reproduced as flaky-under-contention, passed alone and on a serialized re-run; unrelated file, not touched by this diff). `yarn tsc -b --noEmit` and `yarn build` both clean; ran eslint on the four changed files directly, clean. Read the full diff myself: confirmed `mostRecentFalseBreakoutZone` is exported once from metricHelpContent.ts and called identically by both falseBreakoutHelp.interpretValue and PriceChart.tsx's legend (`mostRecentBreakoutZone`), and that the legend's `bars` (historyQuery.data.bars.filter(hasFiniteOhlc)) and the chart-drawing effect's `finiteBars` (same historyQuery.data, same filter) are the same source, so `isFalseBreakoutInRange` windowing can't diverge between legend and chart by construction -- no useMemo/independent recomputation anywhere. Verified the isZoneRelevant intersection math by hand (windowMin=max(ratioMin,spanMin), windowMax=min(ratioMax,spanMax); referencePrice always lies within both source windows since it's the close of the same bar whose high/low feed visibleBarPriceSpan, so windowMin<=windowMax never inverts) and confirmed the new PriceChart.test.tsx/metricHelpContent.test.ts cases actually exercise the fixed behavior (out-of-range caveat text/dimming, and exclusion of a ~40%-away zone on a narrow 2-bar visible span). Accept holds.
